tasks.title: Essay: Language centre outreach priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: In your English class you have been discussing how a language centre can attract more learners from the local community. Now your English teacher has asked you to write an essay.
Write an essay using all the notes and giving reasons for your point of view.

tasks.title: Review: Language centre outreach event
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted!
paragraphs: Have you attended an outreach event organised by a language centre in your area – for example, a conversation club, a cultural workshop or a taster lesson?
Write a review of the event for a specialist magazine about language learning.
Describe what the event involved, say how effective it was at encouraging people to learn the language, and recommend one improvement the centre could make.
The best reviews will be published in next month's issue.

tasks.title: Article: Encouraging local participation
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Our language centre wants to encourage more local residents to take part in our outreach programme.
What would make people in your neighbourhood more interested in learning a new language?
Write an article for the centre's website suggesting one practical way to involve the community, explaining why it would work and what the benefits would be for both learners and the centre.
We will publish the best articles on our website.

tasks.title: Email: Outreach partnership proposal
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Language centre outreach partnership
paragraphs: I am writing on behalf of the Riverside Community Hub. We are interested in partnering with your language centre to offer free introductory workshops for local residents.

Could you tell me what type of workshop you think would be most popular? Also, what practical arrangements would we need to make – for example, about the venue and materials? Finally, do you have any suggestions for how we can encourage people who are usually reluctant to attend such events?
I look forward to your reply.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Marta. You should suggest a workshop type, explain one practical arrangement, and propose a way to attract reluctant participants.
